Engineer by trade and self-describes the mindset: 'as an engineer, you're kind of trained to find faults... oh, what's not right?'

QUALIFIER on the 0.7 confidence: he is not hunting a bargain in the usual sense — he did not ask for a discount and volunteered 'I have that amount'. His stated blocker is a self-spend threshold he has never crossed rather than price-shopping. The structural profile (capable, solo, anchored to a working cheap substitute) matches this avatar better than any other, but the motivation differs from the archetype.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Three structures floated in sequence and none finalised: (1) pay $6,000 upfront or 'you can split it up'; (2) 'fully custom' — a cash-on-hand down payment with the remainder in instalments, sized to whatever the customer can do; (3) third-party financing with interest over 12 months, described only as 'a few hundred dollars' monthly and 'in overall, it's going to be like a bigger sum' — no rate, no provider and no total repayable stated. The prospect declined the financing on principle: 'I probably wouldn't do that just because I don't want to be paying the interest.'

notable.note: The clearest pricing finding in the batch. On hesitation alone — no completed financial picture, no cash-on-hand figure, no monthly surplus, no credit information — the rep invented a 'light version' of the programme at $3,000, half the approved price, delivered by Trevor's head coach Caden rather than by Trevor, and described it as 'everything is almost the same'. The prospect's entire stated reason for being on the call was Trevor personally: he was inspired by Trevor's videos, his philosophy and his physique. His first response to the cheaper tier was to probe the substitute coach's credibility. Elapsed time from '$6,000' to '$3,000' is roughly nine minutes. Separately, this call contains the strongest P4 root-cause work in the batch and the only properly delivered P6a belief question, so the failure is specifically at the money stage, not in the discovery.

quality.notes: Persistent swapping throughout, worsened by the prospect being labelled only by the handle 'smanian'. Whole rep passages sit under the prospect's label — the nutrition question 'Let's go into what nobody likes, which is nutrition' and the golf anecdote 'a lot of guys we have here that play golf' are both the rep but labelled as the prospect. The wife role-play from 00:52:57 to 00:53:45 is scrambled such that the two speakers' lines alternate incorrectly; reconstructed from content, the rep is playing the wife and the prospect is playing himself. The exchange about Caden at 00:51:48 is also inverted — 'I was training with Caden, actually. He was the one training me' is the rep describing his own experience, not the prospect's.
